These disruptive shifts really started about four months ago when I left my structured job to focus on my art therapy certificate, which left my daily routine a lot looser.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of abnormally elevated mood or irritability that lasted for several days or more, where you felt little need for sleep, were more talkative than usual, or engaged in impulsive behaviors?\n\nPatient: Yes, during these high phases over the last four months, I stay up very late working on projects and talk in a nonstop stream that my husband can't even interrupt. During those weeks, I feel a sustained high mood, lots of irritability, and a constant rush of ideas before it eventually gives way to the long, foggy low periods.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any episodes of depression that lasted for at least two weeks, which is a key distinction between some mood disorders?\n\nPatient: Yes, definitely. This current low, foggy period has been hanging around most days for roughly the last three months, which is way longer than two weeks. During this time, my high-energy planning phases have felt directly followed by a steep, foggy crash, and I don't recall having high periods before this that didn't eventually lead into a low phase.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any time in the past when you had a high-energy phase that did not eventually lead to one of these prolonged low, foggy periods, or have all your high-energy phases been followed by a crash like the ones you've described over the last four months?\n\nPatient: This pattern of swinging between intense highs and crashing into foggy lows is actually quite new to me. For me, any period of high energy always leads directly into a steep drop and a prolonged low phase. That foggy, low phase is what I've been stuck in for about three months now."
